statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) — corporate registry online services; NUANS® name search report obtained from an authorized NUANS service provider and submitted by an Alberta-licensed legal practitioner or incorporator
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9, proposed corporate names must be expressed in English and/or French using Latin script; names in non-Latin scripts are not accepted for registration. The name must combine a distinctive element with a mandatory legal element (e.g., 'Limited', 'Incorporated', 'Corporation', 'Ltée', 'Inc.', 'Corp., Ltd.'). No transliteration into other scripts is required; a numbered company ('NNNNNN Alberta Ltd.') avoids name clearance entirely, and non-Latin commercial brand names may be protected separately through trade-mark registration or a provincial assumed business name registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a proposed-name rejection, the incorporator may (1) obtain a fresh NUANS report and resubmit a revised name; or (2) file a written Request for Reconsideration with the Director of Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) within 30 days of the rejection notice, attaching the offending NUANS report, a legal memorandum on distinctiveness and non-misleading character under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), and any ministerial consent or regulator approval already obtained for sensitive tokens. If the Director upholds the rejection, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Alberta Court of King's Bench under the Alberta Rules of Court, Alta. Reg. 124/2010. A new name reservation fee applies upon resubmission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible, with limitations. An Alberta business corporation must maintain a registered office at a physical street address within Alberta during business hours for service of documents; pure mail-forwarding or non-address 'virtual-only' services are non-compliant. For this industry (epoxy resin RPG dice manufacturing), a virtual registered office plus a separate production address is acceptable: the business does not require a public storefront. The production premises, however, must have their own commercial substance (lease or ownership, municipal zoning approval, fire-code compliance, and applicable home-based business authorization if residential), as the provincial registry does not count the production site as the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Registered office: low quantified risk of unannounced inspection (less than 5% annual probability), triggered typically by lender or regulatory verification. Production workspace (epoxy resin handling and casting): moderate risk, approximately 10-20% annual probability of an unannounced visit by municipal fire marshal, Alberta Health Services (AHS), or Alberta OHS (Occupational Health and Safety) authorities, particularly if the workspace is in a mixed-use residential/commercial zone or uses chemical products triggering the Alberta Fire Code and Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS) obligations.

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Service Alberta — Alberta Corporate Registry (Government of Alberta), administered through the Alberta Corporate System (ACCIS) and network of licensed Registry Agents.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA/ARC) is the federal competent tax authority; operational portals are Business Registration Online (BRO) at canada.ca/business-registration, GST/HST NETFILE, and My Business Account (MyBA). Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA on behalf of Alberta under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act and the federal-provincial Tax Collection Agreement; Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax and has no separate sales-tax administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the business corporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act (preferred) or federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act with extra-provincial registration in Alberta; no minimum capital is required. Step 2 - Obtain the federal Business Number (BN), the statutory tax identifier, by applying online through BRO or by submitting Form RC1 to the CRA; simultaneously request the Corporate Income Tax (RD), GST/HST (RC0001), and Import/Export (RM) program accounts. Step 3 - For a foreign entity not incorporated in Canada, appoint a Canadian authorized representative, file Form RC59 (Authorizing or Cancelling a Representative), and submit Form RC1; the CRA will issue a BN and register the non-resident for GST/HST under ETA s. 240(3.1), subject to the same CAD 30,000 small-supplier analysis under ETA s. 148. Step 4 - Register the RM customs program account with the CRA/CBSA for export reporting capability through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS). Step 5 - Maintain the BN program accounts through MyBA, retain all CRA notices of assessment, and keep the GST/HST registration status current for the Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal revenue streams. No separate Alberta corporate income tax registration is required because Alberta participates in the federal Tax Collection Agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Canadian-resident corporation taxed under Part I of the Income Tax Act on worldwide income, plus Alberta corporate income tax of 8% general rate and 2% small-business rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; no pass-through eligibility for a corporation; dividends paid to foreign shareholders are exposed to 25% Part XIII withholding unless reduced by treaty).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Canadian law; corporate taxpayer status is fixed by incorporation and deemed residence under ITA s. 250(2)(a). Available statutory mechanisms: (i) voluntary GST/HST registration for non-residents under ETA s. 240(3.1); (ii) ITA s. 216(1) election permitting a non-resident to file a Part I return on Canadian rental/royalty income instead of Part XIII withholdings; (iii) Part XIV branch-tax planning under ITA s. 219 for a non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada through a permanent establishment, with a 25% branch tax on after-tax Canadian business income subject to treaty relief and the s. 219(3) election; (iv) hybrid-mismatch transitional elections under ITA ss. 18.4-18.7 effective 1 July 2023, relevant where the corporate group uses foreign transparent or check-the-box structures; (v) no election exists to reclassify a corporation as a partnership or disregarded entity for Canadian indirect-tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (ETA); 5% rate applies in Alberta. Alberta is a non-participating province, so the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) does not apply, and Alberta has no provincial retail sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 148(1): a person is not required to register for GST unless total taxable supplies made in Canada (plus worldwide taxable supplies for non-residents carrying on business in Canada, aggregated with associates as applicable, per CRA policy) exceed CAD 30,000 in the current calendar quarter and the four preceding calendar quarters. Voluntary registration is available at any time through ETA s. 240(3.1); Kickstarter pre-sales to Canadian backers count toward the threshold, as do Canada-destination direct sales through Stripe or PayPal.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government-API tax-clearance regime at the federal or Alberta level. Commercial invoices may be paper or electronic but must contain the prescribed ETA information, including the supplier legal name, BN, description of the goods, consideration, rate of GST charged, and zero-rated or exempt status notation. GST/HST returns must be filed through GST/HST NETFILE, and payments are remitted via MyBA or participating financial institutions. Canada participates in the voluntary Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing (PCEI) framework aligned with the Peppol BIS 3.0 four-corner model; the Quebec RPCI B2B e-invoicing mandate rolling from 2026 binds only Quebec-perspective suppliers and is a watch item for multi-province expansion. No pre-clearance approval or digital stamp is required before issuing invoices from Alberta.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of the polyhedral resin tabletop dice qualify as zero-rated supplies under Schedule VI, Part V, s. 20 ETA where the vendor sells and physically exports the goods in a commercial shipment, commercial convoy, or commercial container immediately following the supply, or mails/couriers the goods to a destination outside Canada; the goods must leave Canada within 60 days of the supply per CRA GST/HST Memorandum 17-2, and the supplier must retain transport and customs evidence. Ancillary services (e.g., custom engraving or design services) supplied with export goods may be zero-rated under Sch VI s. 23 where the benefit is realized outside Canada or no part of the service is performed in Canada; royalties or licensing fees from foreign distributors remain subject to 25% Part XIII withholding unless treaty-reduced. Export-heavy operations claim input tax credits (ITCs) on GST paid for resin, molds, packaging, and freight through the GST/HST return, producing a net refund where creditable ITCs exceed output GST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Declaration (Form B13A filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System/CERS) for all consignments meeting export reporting criteria, such as controlled goods or shipments valued over CAD 2,000
CBSA and carrier-ready commercial invoice with full product description, HS classification 9504.90 (games, parlour games, and accessories), unit prices, and non-resident consignee details
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or tracked courier consignment note evidencing the physical exit of the goods from Canada to the foreign backer or distributor
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/FX evidence (SWIFT MT103, bank statement, or Stripe/PayPal settlement record) linking the foreign currency proceeds to the specific export sale
Kickstarter campaign final report, customer destination log, and payment-rail settlement data evidencing the non-resident end-customer supply chain
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA s. 296(1) allows CRA reassessment within four years of the return due date, extended to seven years in cases of misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful default, or fraud; if the export zero-rating is reversed, 5% GST is assessed on the full consideration plus compound prescribed-rate daily interest from the original filing date. ETA s. 285.1 imposes a false-statement penalty equal to the greater of CAD 500 and 25% of the understated net tax or overstated refund; evading-payment prosecutions under ETA s. 280 can yield fines up to 200% of the evaded amount and imprisonment of up to five years on indictment. CRA verification programs data-mine payment-processor (Stripe/PayPal) and Kickstarter settlement records to test export substantiation; common audit triggers are missing B13A/CERS export filings, absent waybills, mismatched customer-residence data, and foreign proceeds collected more than 180 days after shipment without a commercial explanation. The CRA may also impose sanctions for failure to retain proper records; all export evidence, FX receipts, and GST/HST ledgers must be retained for at least six years under ETA record-keeping rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the monetary authority and note-issuing institution; prudential banking supervision and prudential FX balance-sheet oversight rest with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); exchange-control policy is vested in the Minister of Finance/Governor in Council under the Currency Act and the Emergencies Act (dormant); AML/ATF surveillance is executed by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility; since the repeal of the Foreign Exchange Control Act (1951) there are no prior-approval, quota, or licence requirements for dividend remittance, profit repatriation, intercompany loans, capital redemption, or foreign-currency account balances. Practical frictions: (i) every international EFT of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC by the bank and may be held pending source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership documentation; (ii) Part XIII of the Income Tax Act imposes 25% gross withholding on non-resident dividends, interest, and royalties unless reduced by treaty (Canada-US 15%/5% for direct shareholders, Canada-China 10%; treaty relief requires Form NR301 and shareholder residency certificates); (iii) OFAC and Canadian sanctions list screening under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act can freeze flows until cleared; (iv) CDIC deposit insurance covers only CAD 100,000 per depositor per insured institution, so treasury balances above that level require multi-bank spreading.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline; exporters may retain USD, EUR, or CNY balances in bank or EMI multi-currency accounts and convert at commercially agreed spot rates. Compliance boundaries: FINTRAC large-EFT reporting applies to any outbound or inbound wire of CAD 10,000 or more with 24-hour aggregation of structured transfers; foreign-exchange gains and losses are recognized under section 39(1) of the Income Tax Act; GST/HST on qualifying exported goods and services to unregistered non-resident consumers is generally zero-rated when export documentation is maintained.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability rating: C+ (shadow rail only, not treasury-grade). Wise Business, Payoneer, Stripe Treasury, and PayPal Business operate legally in Canada as FINTRAC-registered Money Services Businesses (MSBs) and can aggregate Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal card settlements, but they cannot satisfy Canadian deposit-insurance expectations (no CDIC protection on wallet balances), cannot issue direct SWIFT MT103 messages with capital-injection purpose codes, and their balances represent unsecured claims on the EMI. Legal constraints: MSB registration requires the EMI to maintain a Canadian presence and to comply with PCMLTFA record-keeping, suspicious-transaction, and large-EFT rules; Canadian banks treat third-party EMI payouts as upstream money movements and will request the originator's full platform-reconciliation package before crediting the operating account. Recommended strategy: use the EMI layer as a low-balance pass-through for consumer card capture only, and sweep platform payouts daily into the RBC/TD/BMO operational account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A director's physical attendance is not statutorily mandated in Alberta; the Big-5 banks (RBC, TD, BMO, CIBC, Scotiabank) and ATB permit notarized remote opening with video identity verification, provided the corporation maintains a registered office address in Alberta. Practical expectation: Canadian-resident directors obtain same-week approval; a wholly foreign-held board with no Canadian resident director will typically be asked for an initial in-person sign-off at a Calgary or Edmonton business banking centre, a Canadian-resident Power of Attorney holder, and an enhanced UBO attestation. Onboarding is accelerated when the entity is an ABCA/CBCA corporation and the bank receives the certified articles, business plan, and platform-contract suite before the KYC interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face onboarding with 100% foreign resident directors/shareholders; corporate agent registry address; no physical Alberta office; perceived shell-trading risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of ABCA/CBCA Certificate and Articles; annual return; register of individuals with significant control (CBCA s.21 and Alberta Business Corporations Act equivalent); organizational chart down to natural persons; board resolution authorizing account opening and named signatories; notarized passports and residential proof for all directors; business plan with 12-month cash-flow; physical-presence declaration covering home office or 3PL warehouse; no-PEP status affirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pre-production crowd-funding receipts (Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal) without contemporaneous commercial contracts, deemed unexplained value movement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Crowdfunding campaign URL and valid terms; monthly platform payout statements; itemized contribution-level CSV export; production batch purchase orders; epoxy resin and silicone mold supplier agreements; order-fulfillment carrier bills of lading; returns/refund policy; cash-flow and burn-down model mapping proceeds to Stage 4 liquidity timeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border supplier payables to high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., China, India, UAE) with mismatched purpose versus shipping documents; sanctions exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pro-forma commercial invoices of USD 500 or more each; HS Chapter 32/39 classification codes for resin and pigments; Incoterms 2020 delivery terms; ocean/air waybills; country-of-origin certificates; MT103 chain of prior payments; sanctions screening reports against SEMA and OFAC SDN lists performed by counsel within 30 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Structuring signals: repeated wires near CAD 9,800-9,999; cash deposits; crypto-currency conversions into CAD.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory declaration of source of funds and source of wealth; exchange withdrawal confirmations; full bank and platform ledger for 24 months; board minutes approving each crypto-to-fiat conversion; legal opinion on PCMLTFA ss.9-9.2 and FINTRAC structuring guidance; evidence of full CRA tax reporting of all conversions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unaffiliated third-party disbursements (e.g., affiliate influencers, drop-shipping agents) without service or commission records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed service agreements; vendor KYC file; W-8BEN-E/W-9 and CRA forms for each payee; payment and commission reconciliation sheet per affiliate; evidence of sub-contracted vending activity; attestation that no proceeds were directed to shell or sanctioned persons.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All capital injections must arrive via SWIFT MT103 using SWIFT purpose code GFSR (financial/equity capital) with field 70 reading 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - CA_AB__ISIC_3240 ESCROW ALIAS - BOARD RESOLUTION [DATE]'. The receiving bank must hold a certified board resolution in advance listing the investing shareholder, amount, currency, and funding source; upon receipt the bank files a FINTRAC large-EFT report if the amount is CAD 10,000 or more, and the 24-hour aggregation rule applies to linked transfers. Preferred sequencing: (a) equity injection into the Capital Escrow account; (b) internal journal to the Operational Account; (c) disbursement only against supplier POs and the funding committee's authorized matrix. For a US person shareholder, route the wire through the bank's US clearing entity (RBC/TD/BMO US branch) to avoid correspondent holds; for a Chinese shareholder, settle RMB-CAD through BMO's China desk or a correspondent without a US intermediary; any intercompany debt alternative requires a written loan agreement with CRA prescribed-rate interest and a Part XIII withholding analysis before cash flows mirror.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements: SWIFT MT103 (serial or cover) via RBC/TD/BMO with SWIFT purpose code 301 for goods and 305 for services, with remittance always referencing the commercial invoice number and Incoterms. eCommerce payouts: Stripe/Kickstarter daily auto-sweep into the Operational Account; PayPal used solely for refunds and top-ups. B2B large-ticket payments: for first-time suppliers or values of CAD 250,000 or more, use irrevocable documentary commercial letters of credit (eLC) per UCP600 issued by the Canadian bank. FX conversion is executed on the bank eFX portal at spot pricing with no surrender mandate. Intra-Canada clearing runs through ACSS/LVTS batch credit rails; USD intra-Canada payments use the bank's USD clearing service to avoid double CAD conversion.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX: T+0/T+2 settlement of USD/CAD through the bank eFX portal at interbank-minus-X pip spread, no ISDA required.

Deliverable FX Forwards: physically settled plain-vanilla forwards up to 12-month tenor under the bank's standard Master Forward FX Agreement (CSA-free SME form), notional capped at CAD 5,000,000, used to hedge anticipated Kickstarter USD cash flows.
FX Swaps: tom-next and 1-month rollovers for liquidity management of USD operational balances, documented under the same Master Forward FX Agreement.
Multi-currency operating account netting: USD inflows are netted against USD supplier payables as a natural hedge, converting to CAD only when cash is needed.
Vanilla Currency Options: permissible for larger corporates under a credit-line-collateralized ISDA CSA where forward markets present discontinuous exposure; not recommended at Stage 4 scale.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): legally permissible for exotic-currency receivables but unnecessary for CAD/USD, which is fully convertible; if the bank offers NDF pricing, a deliverable-alternative clause must be included in the Master Forward FX Agreement to avoid an unregulated OTC position.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta, Registry Services Division)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's anniversary date (anniversary of incorporation or of the most recent annual return filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs registry late-processing fees; continued non-filing for two consecutive years triggers Registrar-initiated strike-off or dissolution after notice and statutory reinstatement conditions (retroactive filings plus prescribed fees apply).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation (or of the last annual return), filed electronically through the Corporations Canada online portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years exposes the corporation to Director-initiated dissolution under CBCA s. 236(2) following a 90-day notice period; restoration under s. 241 requires all overdue returns, fees, and a certificate of restoration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit for private, non-reporting corporations; shareholders may unanimously dispense with the auditor. An independent CPA audit is mandatory if the corporation is a reporting issuer (publicly listed or regulated), if the articles, bylaws, or unanimous shareholder agreement require one, or if a bank or lender imposes an audit covenant. For all private companies, shareholder approval of financial statements at each annual meeting remains required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS (mandatory for reporting issuers) or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for eligible private corporations; tax records must satisfy Income Tax Act section 230 retention rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For CBCA federal corporations, the register of individuals with significant control (ISC register) must be created and maintained; each annual return confirms compliance, and any share transfer causing an ISC change must be recorded within 15 days. For Alberta ABCA corporations, no separate provincial UBO filing is currently mandated; annual share-transfer confirmations are evidenced through the completed annual return, the share transfer register, and the declaration of officers respecting record accuracy.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 220-890 per year (CAD 300-1,200) typical Alberta registered office or registered agent range
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable for a private non-reporting corporation that validly waives audit; where a lender or counterparty demands an audit, typical certified audit range is USD 5,900-18,500 (CAD 8,000-25,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% (federal Part I 15% + Alberta general corporate rate 8%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) Small Business Deduction reduces combined federal and Alberta rate to 11% on taxable active business income up to CAD 500,000; scientific research and experimental development (SR&ED) investment tax credits available for qualifying prototyping costs; gross-up and dividend tax credit integration for Canadian-resident shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed via CRA EFILE (for tax preparers) or CRA My Business Account portal; Alberta provincial corporate tax is administered by the CRA and filed as an integrated component of the T2 return with Alberta-specific schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed within six months after the corporation's fiscal period-end. For a non-resident corporation carrying on business in Alberta, the return is due before or on the day that is six months after the end of the fiscal period during which it had a permanent establishment in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal registered name, CRA program account / Business Number (BN), incorporation date, fiscal year-end, and principal business activity codes (NAICS 339930).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must disclose their Canada Revenue Agency program account and any designated permanent establishment(s) in Canada; sales to Canadian end-users through online platforms are reported in the Canadian source schedule where a permanent establishment exists in Alberta.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as net income before taxes under Part I, adjusted by items such as nontaxable capital gains, capital gains allowance to aggregate, non-capital loss carryovers, and other Part I adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident seller, taxable income allocated to Canada can be determined under domestic rules; however, if the corporation has a permanent establishment in Alberta, the income is allocated between Canadian permanent establishments by an agreed formula.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base Part I tax at 15% on taxable income, net of tax reduction provisions, including the Small Business Deduction, manufacturing and processing profits deduction, and general rate reduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents claiming treaty relief must complete and attach Form NR301 or a treaty-based position under section 115; the line 350 amount reflects only income attributable to Canada under the treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta corporate tax at 8% general rate, with a 2% rate for eligible CCPC active business income up to CAD 500,000, and adjustments for interprovincial income allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate shareholder is not allocated Alberta tax on exempt dividend income; only taxable income earned through an Alberta permanent establishment is subjected to provincial allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1 – Net Income (Financial Statements to Tax Return)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciles accounting income to tax basis, adding non-deductible items, subtracting statutory deductions, and incorporating expenses paid to non-residents subject to Part XIII or transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border fees for intellectual property or management services must be arm's-length and documented; non-resident payers must withhold Part XIII tax unless treaty relief and Form NR301 are completed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation schedule for assets, including molds, kilns, and 3D-printing equipment, using prescribed CCA classes and half-year rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporation's Canadian permanent establishment may claim CCA on moveable equipment used in Alberta; careful tracking is required to maintain capital accounts for repatriation purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of the CCPC Small Business Deduction on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; limits reduced by certain passive income thresholds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not available to non-resident corporations or entities controlled by non-resident shareholders unless the non-resident's shareholding is through an eligible CCPC qualifying under Canadian control rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid federal tax plus 1% per full month of delay, capped at 12 months; after 180 days CRA can assess a additional penalty of 1% of chargeable tax. Interest compounds daily on unpaid amounts for both federal and Alberta tax. For failure to file, a director may face criminal penalties if deliberate or under gross negligence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII on dividend paid or deemed paid to non-resident shareholders of a Canadian-resident distribution company.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced dividend withholding tax rate under a Canada income tax treaty, the non-resident shareholder must deliver a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority to the Canadian payor or the CRA, together with a completed Form NR301 (for dividends, interest, royalties, and pensions), NR302 (for indemnities, support payments, and stock options), or NR303 (for 30% and 20% source reductions). For the Canada–US treaty, 5% applies with a 10% voting-stock threshold on shares; for many other treaties, 15% portfolio and 10% at 25% voting threshold. CRA must assess the treaty certificate before a reduced rate is granted; the payor must retain the forms for six years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: 25% Part XIII for royalty payments (including software and royalty for use of brand) and technical service fees; the Canada–US treaty eliminates withholding on certain copyright royalties, 0% on periodic interest, and reduces interest to 0% for arm's length and 15% for non-arm's length. For royalties paid to a US resident, the treaty rate is 10% for industrial royalties; the Canada–US protocol of 2007 generally reduces to 0% for payments that are 'in respect of the acquisition or right to use computer software' and copyrights, but tabletop dice castings are not considered intellectual-property royalties; for a US parent, 25% may be reduced to 15% portfolio or 0% for certain interest. A non-resident recipient must submit a valid TRC and application under section 212 to CRA and complete Form NR301 before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No fixed statutory threshold in CAD; however, CRA's administrative policy waives full contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for SME taxpayers with gross revenues below CAD 10 million and cross-border non-arm's length transactions below CAD 1 million. Above these de minimis thresholds, a local file, master file, and CbC report are required. Transaction-level records and a reasonable-efforts contemporaneous documentation must always exist for any related-party transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not administer an Economic Substance Regulation equivalent to offshore centres (e.g., ESR UAE), but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and the doctrine from the Supreme Court in *Canada Trustco* deny tax benefits for transactions that are primarily tax-motivated and lack substantial economic substance. A corporate payer must demonstrate a real business activity—such as actual casting, shipping, and fulfilment functions in Alberta—if it wishes to claim cross-border treaty benefits or intercompany allocations. Treaty-shopping arrangements are attacked under the treaty anti-abuse provisions, and the CRA expects permanent-establishment countries to correspond to the actual flow of sales revenue from RPG dice manufacturing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting Kickstarter, Stripe, PayPal, or web-shop proceeds from sale of polyhedral dice; claiming fictitious expenses on T2 return; omitting Alberta permanent establishment or cross-border related-party income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Income Tax Act s.239(1), a fine ranging from 50% to 200% of the tax evaded, imprisonment up to 24 months on summary conviction, and up to 5 years if prosecuted by indictment; provincial penalties and gross negligence penalties under s.163.2 may add an additional penalty of up to 50% of the benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be pierö correlative: civil restitution for the tax and penalties, unlimited personal liability for unremitted Part XIII or payroll withholdings upon bankruptcy, and criminal charges as parties to the offence; travel restrictions can be imposed by a court under the bail or recognizance regime pending prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham / Lack of Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Alberta corporation merely as a mail box to invoice intangibles or reposition profits to a low-tax jurisdiction, with no actual manufacturing, economic hiring, or risk assumption in Canada; suppressing the requirement to file a T2 return based on claimed non-residence of the corporation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA will apply the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) to negate non-recognition transactions, disallow treaty benefits, and reassess the true beneficial owner; a sham may be collaterially voided and the corporate veil would be pierced if the entity is a facade. Penalty of 50% of tax benefit under s.163.2 if the offence amounts to careless representation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid tax and penalties under directors' liability certificates; in fraudulent conveyance cases, the court may set aside the corporate limitation and order restitution from director/director's estate; serious cases lead to travel restrictions and imprisonment under criminal fraud provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporation Tax Record-Keeping Failure / Failure to File
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the T2 within six months of the fiscal year-end or failing to retain adequate books and documentation (invoices, shipping logs, inventory records, TP records) as required by s.230 of the Income Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalty of 5% and 1% monthly; failure to provide books and records can lead to a compliance order, criminal contempt, and a default assessment with arbitrary income. For failure to file for more than two years, CRA may issue an automatic assessment and a 5% penalty on underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly allow a default in filing or who are jointly responsible for the failure can be held personally liable for the corporate tax debt under s.227.1 only if funds were not remitted; in wilful cases, personal prosecution as an accessory may attract imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting proceeds from the sale of polyhedral dice through Kickstarter, Stripe, or PayPal while failing to conduct customer due diligence; knowingly using crowdfunding vehicles or PayPal accounts to funnel cash for unrelated illegal activities; or cash transactions above CAD 10,000 without reporting if the business qualifies as a money services business or is engaged in high-risk crowdfunding frauds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), administrative penalties up to CAD 1 million for non-registration or non-compliance; criminal money laundering under Criminal Code s.462.31 carries imprisonment up to 10 years and unlimited fines; false statements to FINTRAC attract penalties up to CAD 500,000 for small businesses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who direct, authorize, or acquiesce in money laundering are criminally liable; civil restitution and asset seizure orders can reach their personal property, and under the Criminal Code the court may order a prohibition from leaving Canada if there is a risk of flight pending sentence.
